liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (3 reviews): A nasty foghorn-like noise during Sugaree nearly burst the listener's eardrum; There were massive sound problems during Sugaree [11][14][16]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Listener loves this Row Jimmy, and finds the Space section truly spacey [13]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): Touch of Grey emerged from Space, and song versions were played pretty well overall [14]
- **Space** (1 review): Listener found Space messed-up and wished Jerry would leave the stage [15]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Bobby sang well in a cluttered, slightly unfocused but harder-rocking, more exciting Hell than the Monterey one [16]
- **Good Time Blues** (1 review): Brent takes a turn with Good Time Blues, which the reviewer finds fairly empty [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd88-08-26 s1t01 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-08-26 s1t02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-08-26 s1t03 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-08-26 s1t04 Never Trust A Woman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-08-26 s1t05 Iko Iko**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-08-26 s1t06 Walkin' Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-08-26 s1t07 When Push Comes To Shove**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-08-26 s1t08 When I Paint My Masterpiece**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-08-26.143125.sbd.ultramatrix.block.blackwood.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 156 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1988-08-26.152393.ultramatrix.miller.fixed.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 157 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1988-08-26.143062.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 157 min [5]. Said about its sound: This recording suffers from severe flutter, addressed with pitch correction settings [5]
- **gd1988-08-26.152078.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 154 min [6]
- **gd88-08-26.schoeps-fob.gardner.8215.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 154 min; rated 2.24/5 by 34 [8]. Said about its sound: The board mix fixed serious imbalances; in the hall Brent's piano swamped the other instruments; Reviewer says the mix in the hall was badly off, and the tape sounds bad too [9][18]

## Around the show

- Santana opened the night with nicely stretched-out songs; the Tacoma Dome was a poor venue and the audience left disappointed [9]
- The walls seemed to soak up the energy; Santana opened and rocked, making a hard act to follow [12]
- Acoustics of the Tacoma Dome were challenging, but the band sounds unlike anywhere else [13]
- Santana played a full two-hour opening set with great sound, while the Dead's sound was poor despite top equipment [14]
- Outside the venue smelled bad; the listener hitchhiked to and from Vancouver [15]
- A first-time attendee ate mushrooms from a stranger; Santana's band opened and the song selection impressed [17]
- Rainy weather and traffic jams outside; Santana was great, but the Dead seemed lost and Jerry out of step [18]
- The Tacoma Dome is built of wood, unlike most domes, so the walls absorb sound [20]
- Listener calls it the worst Dead show attended, partly redeemed by the Eugene show [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-08-26.143125.sbd.ultramatrix.block.blackwood.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Steve Block, Jim Blackwood; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master UltraMatrix Soundboard Dat > Steve Block's cassettes > Jim Blackwood's Dat (16-bit/48k) [1]. Also: Bill Gardner's FOB Schoeps CMC34 recording supplies a short eight-second patch [1]
- **gd1988-08-26.152393.ultramatrix.miller.fixed.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  May 1, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [2]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several ultra masters combined to complete the show, with flutter repaired from an earlier copy [2]
- **gd1988-08-26.143062.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [5]. Also: A patch source came from Bill Gardner [5]
- **gd1988-08-26.152078.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5M [6]. Also: Gardner's FOB Schoeps CMC34 recording supplies a nine-second patch in Drums [6]
- **gd88-08-26.schoeps-fob.gardner.8215.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB Schoeps CMC34 --> Sony PCM-601ES --> DAT [8]
